title: Amnesty: Iran Carried Out 2,159 Executions in 2025 — Highest Since 1981
detail: Amnesty International released findings from its annual Death Penalty Report documenting 2,159 executions in Iran during 2025 — more than double the 2024 figure and the highest recorded number since 1981. Iran's toll was the primary driver behind global executions reaching a 44-year high of 2,707 total worldwide. Amnesty cited Iran's wartime political crackdown, mass prosecution of 2022 protest convicts, and drug-related executions as the key factors. The figures were reported by France 24, CBS News, and other major outlets on May 18, but based on Amnesty data announced May 17. The scale of executions drew condemnation from the UN Human Rights Office.

media.caption: Iran carried out 2,159 executions in 2025 — the highest figure since 1981, driving global executions to a 44-year high

title: Iranian MP Denounces Pezeshkian's Internet Committee as "Decorative"
detail: State-linked outlet Khabar Online quoted MP Mohammad-Reza Pourdehghan criticizing President Pezeshkian's order assigning First VP Aref to lead a committee on ending Iran's internet blackout. The MP called the committee 'more decorative or psychological in nature,' exposing internal fractures within the regime over how to manage public anger at the now 82-day internet shutdown. Security hawks in the IRGC and intelligence establishment held veto power over any connectivity restoration, making the presidential committee largely symbolic. The backlash illustrated the limits of reformist influence in Pezeshkian's government amid wartime emergency measures.

media.caption: Iran's tiered internet system leaves most citizens in the dark 82 days into the war-era blackout
